# package slcan

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canbus/slcan"
```

Package slcan is a CAN transport over the serial-line CAN protocol (LAWICEL ASCII, "slcan") of USB-to-CAN adapters such as the CANable, CANtact, USBtin and LAWICEL CANUSB, without the Linux slcan driver: it works on every operating system go-serial supports and over any byte stream (a pseudo-terminal, a TCP connection to a serial server).

Frames are text records ended by "\\r": "t1232A1B2" is a standard data frame 123 with two bytes, "T" an extended one, "r"/"R" remote frames and "d"/"D"/"b"/"B" CAN FD frames without and with bit rate switch (the extension of the CANable 2.0 firmware). Open sends "C" (close), the bit rate ("S0".."S8", "Y2"/"Y5" for the CAN FD data phase) and "O" (open) or "L" (listen only); Close sends "C". Adapter replies ("\\r", "\\a", "z", "Z") and records that are not frames are skipped.

Adapters that report their status send "e" records (bus errors, such as "e1a" for an ACK error) and "s" records (controller state and error counters, such as "sp130012"); a Conn turns them into error frames exactly as the Linux slcan driver does, delivered when the filters' ErrorMask selects them. The protocol has no error state indicator and no echo of sent frames; receive timestamps are taken on arrival.

A peer that stops reading cannot hold up a Conn: when the byte stream has write deadlines (SetWriteDeadline, as a net.Conn or a pollable \*os.File has), Send ends at its context's deadline or cancellation; on any stream, Close gives the closing "C" at most 100 ms and then closes the stream, which ends a blocked write. On a stream without write deadlines a write blocked on such a peer ends only when Close closes the stream.

## Variables

```go
var Bitrates = map[int]string{
	10000: "S0", 20000: "S1", 50000: "S2", 100000: "S3", 125000: "S4",
	250000: "S5", 500000: "S6", 750000: "S7", 1000000: "S8", 83300: "S9",
}
```

Bitrates are the nominal bit rates of the S commands.

```go
var DataBitrates = map[int]string{2000000: "Y2", 5000000: "Y5"}
```

DataBitrates are the CAN FD data phase bit rates of the Y commands of the CANable 2.0 firmware.

## Functions

### func AppendFrame

```go
func AppendFrame(dst []byte, f *canbus.Frame) ([]byte, error)
```

AppendFrame appends the slcan record of f, terminated by "\\r", to dst: "t" (standard data), "T" (extended data), "r"/"R" (remote), "d"/"D" (CAN FD) or "b"/"B" (CAN FD with bit rate switch). A classical frame's DLC 9..15 is sent as 8. Error frames and CAN FD frames with the error state indicator cannot be expressed: they return [canbus.ErrUnsupported](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrUnsupported).

### func ParseErrorRecord

```go
func ParseErrorRecord(line []byte, f *canbus.Frame) (bool, error)
```

ParseErrorRecord parses an "e" record, in which an adapter reports bus errors: "e", the number of error codes (0-8) and one letter per error — a (ACK), b (bit 0), B (bit 1), c (CRC), f (form), o (RX overrun), O (TX overrun) or s (stuff). For example "e3bcO" reports a bit 0 error, a CRC error and a TX overrun. It fills f with the error frame the Linux slcan driver delivers for the record. It reports false, without error, for a line that is not an "e" record. As in Linux, characters after the codes are ignored and a record has at least three characters.

### func ParseFrame

```go
func ParseFrame(line []byte, f *canbus.Frame) (bool, error)
```

ParseFrame parses one slcan line (without its "\\r") into f. It reports false, without error, for lines that are not frames: acknowledgements ("", "z", "Z"), commands a host sends (O, C, L, S6, ...) and status or version replies. A frame may be followed by a four-digit timestamp (the Z1 option of LAWICEL adapters); it is ignored.

### func ParseStateRecord

```go
func ParseStateRecord(line []byte) (st canbus.State, txErrors, rxErrors int, ok bool, err error)
```

ParseStateRecord parses an "s" record, in which an adapter reports its controller state and error counters: "s", the state — a (error active), w (warning), p (passive) or b (bus off) — and the receive and transmit error counters as three decimal digits each. For example "sp130012" reports error passive with 130 receive and 12 transmit errors. It reports false, without error, for a line that is not an "s" record. The record has exactly eight characters, as recent Linux versions require (older ones ignore characters after the counters).

### func StateFrame

```go
func StateFrame(prev, st canbus.State, txErrors, rxErrors int) (canbus.Frame, bool)
```

StateFrame returns the error frame the Linux slcan driver delivers when a state record moves the controller from prev to st, with the record's error counters. It reports false when the state did not change: Linux then delivers nothing, even if the counters did. Counters above 255 do not fit the frame and wrap, as in Linux.

## Types

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Bitrate sets the nominal bit rate (a key of [Bitrates]); 0 keeps
	// the adapter's setting.
	Bitrate int
	// DataBitrate sets the CAN FD data phase bit rate (a key of
	// [DataBitrates]); 0 sends none.
	DataBitrate int
	// ListenOnly opens the channel with "L": the adapter neither sends nor
	// acknowledges frames.
	ListenOnly bool
	// NoCommands sends no setup or close commands: for a peer that is not
	// an adapter, such as the Linux slcan line discipline or another
	// program.
	NoCommands bool
	// Name is the interface name (default "slcan").
	Name string
	// QueueSize is the number of received frames held for Receive
	// (default 1024); more are dropped and counted.
	QueueSize int
}
```

Config configures a Conn.

### type Conn

```go
type Conn struct {

	// closed by Close
	// closed when the reader stops
	// wsem is held by the one write in progress; a channel rather than
	// a mutex so that waiting for it honours a context, and Close can
	// skip it.

	// partial: a write ended part way through a record, so the next
	// record starts with "\r" to end the fragment.

	// guards state, txErrs, rxErrs

	// txErrs and rxErrs are the error counters of the last state record.

	// why the reader stopped, set before ended closes
	// polled: rw's reads time out, so Close waits for the reader before
	// closing it (a serial port must not be closed during a read).

}
```

Conn is a CAN transport over slcan. It implements [canbus.Transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Transport).

#### func New

```go
func New(rw io.ReadWriteCloser, cfg Config) (*Conn, error)
```

New starts a Conn on rw, which it owns: Close closes it. Unless cfg.NoCommands, it first sends the setup commands.

#### func Open

```go
func Open(device string, baud int, cfg Config) (*Conn, error)
```

Open opens a serial adapter at device (for example /dev/ttyACM0 or COM3) with the given serial baud rate (0: 115200; USB adapters ignore it) and starts a Conn on it.

#### func (Conn) Capabilities

```go
func (c *Conn) Capabilities() canbus.Capabilities
```

Capabilities describes slcan: CAN FD (with adapters that support it) and error frames (from adapters that send "e" and "s" records); no hardware filters, timestamps or echoes.

#### func (Conn) Close

```go
func (c *Conn) Close() error
```

Close sends "C" (unless NoCommands) and closes the device. It does not wait on the peer: the "C" is skipped while a Send is writing and given at most 100 ms otherwise; the device is closed regardless, which ends a write still blocked. Once the device is gone, errors of closing it are not reported.

#### func (Conn) Drops

```go
func (c *Conn) Drops() (uint64, canbus.DropReason)
```

Drops returns the frames lost because Receive was not called fast enough.

#### func (Conn) Name

```go
func (c *Conn) Name() string
```

Name returns the interface name.

#### func (Conn) Receive

```go
func (c *Conn) Receive(ctx context.Context, f *canbus.Frame) error
```

Receive waits for the next frame. Once the device is gone it returns an error wrapping [canbus.ErrInterfaceDown](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrInterfaceDown).

#### func (Conn) Send

```go
func (c *Conn) Send(ctx context.Context, f *canbus.Frame) error
```

Send writes a frame. It returns once the record is written to the device; the protocol does not confirm transmission on the bus.

#### func (Conn) SetFilters

```go
func (c *Conn) SetFilters(fs canbus.FilterSet) error
```

SetFilters sets the filters, applied in software as records arrive. As with SocketCAN, a Conn delivers every data frame and no error frames until filters are set; error frames are delivered when their class is in the set's ErrorMask.

#### func (Conn) State

```go
func (c *Conn) State() (st canbus.State, txErrors, rxErrors int)
```

State returns the controller state and error counters of the last "s" record (error active with zero counters until one arrives). Adapters that send no state records always report error active.

#### func (Conn) Stats

```go
func (c *Conn) Stats() canbus.Stats
```

Stats returns the counters. RxErrors counts delivered error frames, RxFailure malformed records.
